<reason>Both sides were sharp and the clash narrowed well, but PRO built the cleaner route to victory. CON's strongest structural move was to exclude PRO's evidence as recolonisation or park cases and demand a genuine release-over-objection example; PRO answered that pressure question squarely with Idaho, Mexican wolves, Jura/Slovenian lynx, and Scottish sea eagles, meeting the burden CON set. PRO's own pressure question—what happens when the cheque is refused—drew from CON an answer ("move, redesign, fund the cull properly") that PRO credibly recast as the century-old failed status quo CON had already conceded in its opening. CON's "no author" and founder-population points were inventive, and the Idaho cull/EU downgrade counterattack landed a real hit, but PRO's reply that no recovered population has been removed and that "grumbling does not browse saplings" held. CON's closing pivot to "ecological function requires dense predators" was its best framing, but it arrived late and unsupported against PRO's examples of populations in the hundreds or thousands. PRO made the decision easier: predators-plus-grumbling versus conceded, ongoing degradation.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's A1 in Rebuttal 2 ([B4.1]-[B4.3]) directly met CON's "name one case" challenge with Idaho and several others, then flagged that CON's question was constructed to exclude every category of success—this neutralised CON's central "consent is the delivery mechanism" claim and forced CON onto the weaker "hunted populations don't function" ground.</best_rebuttal>
